structure: repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend is the high-risk plants notification frontend (Node, Hapi, Nunjucks, GOV.UK Frontend) on the shared journey platform. The set mounts through src/server/app/routes-high-risk-plants.js (113 lines) and lives in src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants (set.js; journeys/linear with config.js, features/, flow/ and parties/; obligations/ with one file per section; services/commodities; spec/ with the decisions ledger; docs/ with recipe docs). Each page is a feature folder under journeys/linear/features holding page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, often fields.js, evaluation.js and a view-model folder, and one *.fit.spec.js (in-process page test). The journey order is flow/flow.js: start (dashboard), commodity (commodity type, commodities list), commodityDetails (commodity details sub-page), origin, arrival (arrival status, arrival details), destination (place of destination), parties (consignor, identification numbers), contact (consignment contact), and review (check answers, declaration, confirmation), with the hub (task list) and the dashboard's row actions (delete notification, cancel or amend) outside the sections. Feature folders are 100 to 1,300 lines each with their fit spec; the in-scope code, templates, copy and fit specs come to roughly 14,000 lines, plus the 1,433-line spec/decisions.json ledger (84 decisions). src/server/app/shared (about 940 lines outside its tests) holds layout.njk, kit.js, save-actions.njk, section-caption.njk, error-summary.njk, error.njk, set-context.js, paths.js and the shared copy (copy.js, copy-leaves.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js). The scope leaves out: unit tests (*.test.js, which repeat what the controllers and fit specs show), the journey platform outside the set and shared folders (engine/, flow/, bridge/, model/, services/persistence/, analysis/, auth/), sets/high-risk-plants/docs (developer recipes), and spec/journey-spec.json, spec/conflicts.json, spec/backlog-extras.json and spec/panel/ (the panel's evidence; spec/panel/README.md says decisions.json is the only place a ruling lives). It is cut into 9 parts by what a user sees: shared layout and kit, the flow and hub, the dashboard with its row actions, the commodity pages, origin and arrival, destination and consignor pickers, identification numbers and contact, the review pages, and the decisions ledger.

parts.title: Shared layout, kit, save actions and copy
parts.scope: Everything in src/server/app/shared outside its *.test.js files, plus the set's mount and config (set.js, journeys/linear/config.js, routes-high-risk-plants.js). It stops at any one page's own template or copy: those belong to the page's part.
covers: The page layout in layout.njk: header, service name, navigation, phase banner, footer, back link, language toggle, title pattern and every block a page fills
Every helper kit.js gives pages (form fields, radios, summary rows, buttons and their GOV.UK component options)
The save actions every question page shows (save-actions.njk): each button and link, its text and where it goes
The section caption, error summary and error page templates: their headings and wording
Every shared copy string in copy.en.js and its Welsh counterpart in copy.cy.js, verbatim
The set's id, base path, layout and session cookie names (set.js, config.js), and how the set mounts and guards entry (routes-high-risk-plants.js, set-context.js, paths.js)

parts.title: Journey flow, run, task rows and hub
parts.scope: The journey's page order, the opening run, the task rows and their statuses, the entry guard, section captions, the obligation set index, the feature registry, and the hub (task list) page with its fit spec and the section caption fit spec. It stops at each section's own pages and obligation section files, which belong to the parts that own those pages.
covers: The 9 sections in flow.js in order, the pages in each, the review gate and the flow-only keys, with the ordering rules its comment states
The opening run's steps (RUN_STEPS in run.js) and where Continue goes after each
Every task row in task-rows.js: its label, the pages it covers, its status values and how each status is worked out
Every entry guard redirect in entry-guard.js and the condition that fires it
Every section caption and its Welsh counterpart
The hub page: its route, heading, caption, every task row link, status tag, and button or link, with its copy verbatim, and every test in hub.fit.spec.js and section-caption.fit.spec.js
The registered routes and dispatch pages in features/index.js, and the obligation set's sections as obligations/index.js lists them

parts.title: Dashboard, row actions, delete and cancel or amend
parts.scope: The notification list (dashboard) with its sorting, row view model, row actions and late tag, plus the two row-action pages it links to: delete notification and cancel or amend. It stops at the journey pages a row's open or change action leads into.
covers: The dashboard page: its route, heading, start button, table columns, every status and tag (including the late tag), sort options and their order, pagination or empty state, and its copy verbatim in English and Welsh
Every row action in view-model/row/actions.js: its text, which statuses show it, and where it leads
The delete notification page: route, heading, question, options, buttons, error message verbatim and what happens on each answer
The cancel or amend page: route, heading, question, options, buttons, error message verbatim and what happens on each answer
Every test in dashboard.fit.spec.js, delete-notification.fit.spec.js and cancel-amend.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Commodity type, commodities list and commodity details
parts.scope: The commodity section: the commodity type question, the commodities list page, the commodity details entry sub-page, the commodity line form and links, the commodity data service and the commodity obligation section. It stops at origin.
covers: The commodity type page (every file in commodity-type/ except *.test.js): route, heading, caption, every option, hint, error message verbatim, what it saves and where each answer leads
The commodities list page: route, heading, table or summary list columns, add, change and remove links, empty state, Continue and its error messages verbatim
The commodity details page: route, heading, every field with its label, hint, options, limits and whether it is required, every validation rule with its error message verbatim, and where save returns
The commodity data the service offers (services/commodities/index.js) and how pages search or list it
Every obligation in obligations/sections/commodity.js: what it requires, its gates and scope
Every test in commodity-type.fit.spec.js, list.fit.spec.js and details.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Origin, arrival status and arrival details
parts.scope: The origin page, the arrival status question and the arrival details page, with their timing windows, arrival bounds and obligation sections. It stops at the place of destination.
covers: The origin page: route, heading, caption, every field with label, hint and options (and how the country list is shown), every error message verbatim, and what it saves
The arrival status page: route, heading, every status option and hint, error message verbatim, which commodity types skip it, and where each answer leads

The arrival details page: route, heading, every field (dates, times, ports, transport and others) with label, hint, format, limits and whether it is required, every validation and bounds rule with its error message verbatim, and how fields change with the arrival status
The timing windows and arrival bounds the pages enforce
Every obligation in obligations/sections/origin.js and arrival.js
Every test in origin.fit.spec.js, arrival-status.fit.spec.js and arrival-details.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Place of destination and consignor pickers
parts.scope: The two address book picker pages that start the destination and parties sections: place of destination and consignor, with the shared address-book-picker helpers and the destination obligation section. It stops at identification numbers and the consignment contact, which are part 7, though part 7 also reads the picker helpers.
covers: The shared address book picker (address-lines.js, render.js, pagination.js, view-model.js): how an address entry is shown, page size, pagination and empty state

The place of destination page: route, its three questions and which arrival status shows each, heading, hint, every option, search or pagination control, links to add an address, error messages verbatim and what it saves
The consignor page: route, heading, hint, every option, pagination, links, error messages verbatim and what it saves
Every obligation in obligations/sections/destination.js
Every test in place-of-destination.fit.spec.js and consignor-select.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Identification numbers and consignment contact
parts.scope: The rest of the parties section and the contact section: the identification numbers page, the consignment contact picker, the parties helper and the parties and contact obligation sections. The address-book-picker helpers are read for context only: part 6 claims them.
covers: The identification numbers page: route, heading, every field with label, hint, format, limits and whether it is required, every error message verbatim, and what it saves
The consignment contact page: route, heading, hint, every option, pagination, links, error messages verbatim and what it saves
How unresolved party references are handled (parties/index.js)
Every obligation in obligations/sections/parties.js and contact.js
Every test in identification-numbers.fit.spec.js and consignment-contact-select.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Check answers, declaration and confirmation
parts.scope: The review section: check your answers (notification view), declaration and confirmation, with the lateness rules they share and the review obligation section. It stops at the dashboard the confirmation links back to.
covers: The check answers page: route, heading, every summary card or section and row in order, each row's key, value format and change link, outstanding-party messages, the submit or continue button and any warning, with copy verbatim
The declaration page: route, heading, declaration text, checkbox or button, error message verbatim and what submitting does
The confirmation page: route, panel title and body, reference shown, what happens next text and links
The lateness rules in review/lateness.js and how each review page shows them
Every obligation in obligations/sections/review.js
Every test in check-answers.fit.spec.js, declaration.fit.spec.js and confirmation.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Decisions ledger
parts.scope: The set's rulings ledger, spec/decisions.json: 84 decisions, each stamped on a conflict or behaviour. The panel README is read for how the ledger works; the panel's evidence files (rulings.json, critic.json) are out of scope.
covers: Every one of the 84 decisions in decisions.json: its id, subject, ruling, resolution and rationale, who decided it and when, and whether it is superseded, quoted by id and words
The standing rulings the panel README names (what is out of phase and parked)
